title: FancyZones Issue with msedge.exe Apps
author: JStockCo
summary: FancyZones treats distinct Edge PWAs as the same app for last-known-zone placement, matching the older open Chromium Edge PWA tracker.

status.label: Existing PWA placement tracker
status.detail: Open Issue 652 already tracks supporting Chromium Edge PWAs separately for the last-known-zone feature, and Issue 34713 was consolidated there with the same AUMID direction.

next_action.label: Post duplicate guidance
next_action.reason: Route the new Edge PWA details to the existing FancyZones PWA tracker instead of requesting a new diagnostic first.

judgment.rationale: The report describes the same FancyZones last-known-zone PWA identity problem already tracked by Issue 652. The code stores app-zone history keyed by app path/process identity, and the reporter’s proposed AUMID or browser app-id direction belongs on the existing tracker rather than a new design fork.
evidence: The reporter has around a dozen Edge PWAs, and one PWA can open in the zone last used by another PWA.
The body identifies shared msedge.exe or msedge_proxy.exe hosting and suggests Edge app ID or AUMID as the distinguishing key.
Issue 652 remains open for FancyZones last-known-zone support for Chromium Edge PWAs.
Issue 34713 described Chrome/PWA windows being treated as the same program and was closed as a duplicate of Issue 652 after AUMID/AppZoneHistory discussion.
AppZoneHistory.cpp serializes app-zone history under appPath and GetAppLastZoneIndexSet uses process path, consistent with the shared-browser-process failure mode.
judgment.recommended_action: Post duplicate/consolidation guidance pointing to Issue 652 in plain text and ask the reporter to add Edge-specific AUMID/window identity observations there.

issue_context.summary: Distinct Edge PWAs appear to share FancyZones last-known-zone placement state because they are hosted by Edge processes, a scenario already tracked for Chromium Edge PWAs.
known_information: The issue reproduces on PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 with three Dell S2721DS displays.
The reporter uses around a dozen installed Edge PWAs.
Different PWAs can open in the zone most recently used by another PWA.
Issue 652 remains open for FancyZones last-known-zone support for Chromium Edge PWAs.
Issue 34713 was closed as a duplicate of Issue 652 and includes an AUMID/AppZoneHistory direction.
inferences: The new report likely represents another instance of the existing PWA identity gap rather than a new standalone FancyZones regression.
The suggested AUMID or browser app ID evidence may be useful on the canonical tracker, but it is not necessary to keep this duplicate issue open.
issue_context.analysis: The live issue body supplies enough detail to match the existing tracker. Consolidating avoids duplicate design work while preserving the reporter’s Edge-specific details as useful implementation context.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full live issue body, comments, labels, assignees, timeline, and closed-by-PR references.
Reviewed Issue 652 and Issue 34713 as historical duplicate/design context.
Inspected FancyZones AppZoneHistory.cpp, where last-known-zone history is stored and retrieved by app path/process identity.

actions.label: Close as duplicate of FancyZones PWA tracker

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed Edge PWA description and the AUMID/app-id suggestion. This matches the existing FancyZones tracker for Chromium Edge PWAs and last-known-zone placement in Issue 652; a later equivalent Chrome/PWA report, Issue 34713, was also consolidated there and includes the same AUMID direction. Please add your Edge-specific examples and any identity details to Issue 652 so the implementation discussion stays in one place.
